subject: Clarify VAT treatment (threshold check) and invoice routing for Q2 billing
messages:
From: A. Singh <asingh@ecosupply.co.uk>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 14:12:00 +0100
Subject: VAT charge question for Q2 invoice

Hi Sofia,

Quick question — our accounts team noticed the invoice draft for April/May includes VAT charged on the platform fees. Helios Systems is a UK registered business (we have a UK VAT reg), but we also have an Irish subsidiary that handles EU orders. Can you confirm whether Redwood should be applying reverse-charge (0% on B2B) or charging Irish VAT at 23% given our split setup? We attached our VAT cert for reference.

We want to avoid any retro corrections if possible — what evidence do you need from our side to validate reverse-charge? Also, can invoices be split between platform and marketplace fees for tax treatment?

Thanks,
Amit Singh
Head of Finance, Helios Systems
attachments: helios_vat_certificate.pdf
From: sofia_ivanova@redwood.com
To: A. Singh <asingh@ecosupply.co.uk>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 18:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: VAT charge question for Q2 invoice

Hi Amit — thanks for flagging and for the VAT cert. Short answer: we can apply reverse-charge (no VAT on Redwood invoice) provided: (1) we validate a valid VAT ID for the legal entity receiving the service and (2) place-of-supply rules show the customer is a VAT-registered business in the EU/UK for these B2B services.

Next steps from our side:
- Finance will validate the VAT ID against VIES and internal registry (Ben).
- If the ID validates and maps to the invoice entity, we will reissue the invoice with reverse-charge language and zero VAT.
- If the ID does not validate or the billed entity is the Irish subsidiary that is not the VAT-registered purchaser for this contract, we may need to charge Irish VAT and split the invoice accordingly.

Can you confirm which legal entity (Helios Systems Ltd, UK VAT XXXXXX) should be billed for platform fees, and whether your Irish entity is only for EU order routing? If you can confirm the billing legal entity and resend the VAT cert stamped/dated, we aim to reissue within two business days.

Proposed temporary plan (to avoid payment delays): we can accept payment of the net amount while we put the VAT amount in suspense and re-route once validated. That avoids overdue dunning while we confirm. Will that work for you?

Best,
Sofia 
Sofia Ivanova
Revenue Operations Manager | Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — a couple of additional points from tax/compliance:
- We should capture the claimant evidence (VAT cert PDF, VIES lookup printout, confirmation email from customer) in the invoice attachment bucket and reference it on the invoice (e.g., "VAT reverse charge applied — customer VAT ID validated on 2027-05-10").
- For cases where we split invoices: provide separate invoice lines with clear descriptions (platform fee — reverse charge; marketplace fee — VAT charged at point of sale). That makes downstream reconciliation and VAT reporting easier.
- If the customer prefers the suspense route, we need a cut-off to hold VAT for no more than 30 days before making a determination to avoid accounting open-item aging issues.

I'll draft the reissue language and the snippet to be added to the invoice footer. Ben — please link FIN-2789 PR to the NetSuite transaction once it's created.

-Marissa

Hi Amit — quick update and proposed resolution:

1) Billing entity: please confirm that invoices should be made out to Helios Systems Ltd (UK) — VAT GB999999999 — and provide the company registration number.
2) Evidence accepted: your attached helios_vat_certificate.pdf and our VIES check show an active UK VAT registration; please confirm the billing legal entity matches the cert.
3) Invoice action: once you confirm, we will:
   - Reissue the April invoice with reverse-charge language and 0% VAT on the platform fees (line item tax code RC-EU).
   - Split the invoice so that marketplace commissions (if any) remain charged with applicable VAT.
   - Post the VAT amount into suspense pending your confirmation if you go with temporary payment option; otherwise reissue immediately and request payment for net amount.
4) Timeline: we will issue the reissued invoice and attach the VIES validation record by end of business Wed (2027-05-12).

If you prefer, we can also run a one-time self-bill for the quarter to align your accounts payable cutoffs. Let me know which route you prefer; if we don't hear back by EOD Wed we'll hold VAT in suspense and proceed with the reissue once we have the confirmation.

Best regards,
Sofia
